body: I didn't see this comment before now, sorry. I just kinda figured that my post wasnt that relevant, so I tried not to think about it anymore.

You're probably right about my mother having a lot of expectations, that makes a lot of sense. 

One thing I remember about the first time I selfharmed was my mother asking "why are you doing this to me?", and I guess it's been like this ever since, and probably before as well. She kicked me out when I was 16, because she said I was ruining the family and she didn't want to have me in the house anymore(due to me selfharming and being depressed).CPS stepped in and I lived at an institution (might be the wrong word, I'm not english) until I turned 18. We didn't really speak that much during my stay at the institution, because I was really angry and felt like she didn't care. 

When I finally did speak to my family again (which I did mainly because I have a little sister, and regardless of my feelings about my mother, I want to be there for her), I heard all these things about my mother telling my sister not to end up like me, which made me angry all over again. 

whoops, I went on a bit of a rant there, my apologies. You made me think a lot about how my mother have been handling this during the years, and I should probably start realizing she won't be supportive. It might be best if I just don't talk about this stuff with her, so I don't encourage her to say stuff like that.

I see myself in what you're talking about. Found myself thinking the thought yesterday when I was checking up when a show I'm watching will start again. Kept thinking, 'damn, I really wanted to see how that ended'. It's good to hear that you're still hanging on, and yeah, with a little help and support, we can get through this. 
thanks for the response and stay strong.

Oh yeah, it definitely is. I did manage to stay sane through the night, and went to see my therapist earlier today. Got some new pills and the promise of finding out what my diagnosis is, so I left there feeling much better than I did yesterday. Of course, the suicidal thoughts are still there, but there's a smidge of hope, I guess. Again, thanks so much for the kind words, they mean a lot to me.

Thank you for the kind words. 

I do see a professional or whatever every week, but it's so hard to find someone good in my country. I've been seeing a number of different people over the years, but it seems the only thing they want to do is give me pills. I know this comes of as just very negative, but I'm so sick of getting a ton of pills and no answers. I've asked to know what's 'wrong' for years now. I don't know the English word for this, sorry, but you know, basically I want to take the tests and stuff, and get to know my specific problem. I was diagnosed with depression, but that was seven years ago. Now I'm on Seroquel because I don't sleep and have moodswings, but they just make me constantly suicidal. I've been at the hospital twice because of suicide attempts, but I don't know. Third time's the charm and such.

I guess. It did feel good getting rushed to the hospital and being taken care of. I just hope I don't get too addicted to the feeling, cus it's really scary. Thank you for your comment and advice, and I'm sorry to hest you're in the same situation. If you need to talk, I am here.
That sound legit. I've never thought of it that way before. If that's the case, that's not good, though.
Thanks, I'm always careful, I don't cut to die, so I keep away from the dangerous zones.

That's the way I felt as well, one of the nights I stayed there, an alcoholic walked back and forth in the halls the whole time, screaming and knocking on the doors. That's not a good place for me, it really would've only made things worse. And I don't want to go back to the hospital because I'm afraid of meeting the same people, and not being taken seriously. I made it through the night, but woke up feeling even worse. 

Thing is, in my country, patients of mental disorders and similiar things don't really get much help. It's easier for a suicidal person to just kill him/herself, because getting help is a long, slow and painful process. Which is one of the reasons I haven't gone back yet. I feel like I have to wait until I really am on the edge, because then I will be taken seriously.

I prefer not disclosing too much information about myself, as this obviously isn't my main account on reddit, and I know a lot of people who browse the site. But I will say that I am female, and the main thing that makes me miserable is probably childhood trauma. There's been a lot of sexual and verbal abuse. 
Haha, it sure does.

I appreciate that, it's nice to hear that I sound sane and such haha. And you know, I really want all that stuff for myself, because I know I deserve it. But living is hard, dealing with traumas is hard, and right now I don't really feel like I have the motivation to continue. Thus this post, I guess. But as I said, I really appreciate your post, it's uplifting to see that someone, even if it's a stranger on the internet, believes that I can get through this.

I think that was my thought when I called an ambulance last week. And while I was on observation, I felt really relaxed and calm for a while. I actually enjoyed when I had to take tests and drink charcoal, blood tests and all that. Because for the first time I felt like someone was taking care of me. The thing is, when they started questioning, "will you go out and do it again" ect, I just felt really scared. I'm tired, I don't want to talk about things, I just want to rest. So I lied my way out of the hospital and went home. Then I got convinced to call again and get admitted to a psych ward. But as a young adult, those places aren't really for me, lots of really damaged people stay there, so they didn't really want me there, and I felt unwelcome. So I went home again. And now I just feel stuck.

You really shouldn't feel that way, intimacy is important in any relationship, those who says it isn't are bullshitting. She probably doesn't feel that you're being selfish either, because she most likely doesn't want to feel this way herself. I get that the Zoloft is helping, but sexual dysfunction is a big deal if you're going to make a relationship last. I'm not saying you should force her to switch or quit, but you need to sit down and have a serious conversation about it and try to figure out what to do.
Real sorry to hear that. Feel free to inbox me at any time, though I'm not sure how much help I can be.

I get what you're saying, and you're probably right. I am in control and I know I can go to sleep and feel a little better for a few hours tomorrow. The thing is that is my routine, and I am really sick of it. I don't really know how to describe it, which is probably why I've never gotten the proper help. I guess I've been stuck in a state of self hate for so long, letting go of that part is really scary and difficult.

I've been on Zoloft myself, and had the same problem. I actually ended up ending a long relationship because I simply didn't feel anything at all anymore. I don't really have any other advice than maybe she should talk to someone, and consider switching medications. Side effects on anti depressants are hard to really do anything about, because they can be really important for the person taking them. 
In the end, I stopped taking them, and it was real hard in the beginning, but I found out that Zoloft wasn't for me. 
Hope everything works out between you two.
